title: Azure Files and File Shares
description: Understand Azure Files, SMB and NFS protocols, and Azure File Sync for hybrid cloud scenarios.

data.text: Azure Files is a fully managed file share service that you can access using the standard Server Message Block (SMB) protocol or Network File System (NFS). It's like having a network drive in the cloud that multiple machines can connect to at the same time.

data.title: Protocol Comparison
items: **SMB (Server Message Block)** — The standard Windows file sharing protocol. Works with Windows, macOS, and Linux. Supports Azure Active Directory authentication.
**NFS (Network File System)** — Common in Linux and Unix environments. Provides better performance for Linux workloads but has fewer authentication options.

data.text: Azure File Sync lets you centralize your file shares in Azure while keeping the convenience of accessing them on your local Windows servers. It caches frequently used files locally and syncs changes to the cloud automatically.

data.title: Why Use Azure Files?
data.text: Azure Files replaces on-premises file servers without requiring you to rewrite your applications. Your existing apps can connect to the file share using the same SMB or NFS APIs they already use.

terms.definition: A shared folder accessible over the network using SMB or NFS
A service that syncs on-premises Windows file servers with Azure Files
A logical grouping of Azure file shares and registered servers that sync with each other

data.title: Create an Azure File Share with Azure CLI
data.content: This example creates an SMB file share and connects to it from a Windows machine.
data.code:
# Create a storage account (if you don't have one)
az storage account create \
  --name mystorageaccount123 \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --location eastus \
  --sku Standard_LRS \
  --kind FileStorage

# Create a file share
az storage share create \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --name myshare

# List files in the share
az storage file list \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --share-name myshare

# Upload a file to the share
az storage file upload \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123 \
  --share-name myshare \
  --source ./myfile.txt \
  --path myfile.txt

# Create an SMB access token for mounting
az storage account keys list \
  --resource-group myResourceGroup \
  --account-name mystorageaccount123

data.title: Try It Yourself
data.description: Create your own file share in Azure and upload a document to it.
steps: Open Azure Cloud Shell and create a resource group
Create a storage account with FileStorage kind
Upload a local text file to the share
List the contents of the share to confirm the upload
data.expectedOutcome: You should see your uploaded file listed in the share contents.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Azure Files provides managed file shares via SMB and NFS
SMB is best for Windows and mixed environments
NFS is better for Linux workloads
Azure File Sync bridges on-premises and cloud file storage
data.takeaway: Azure Files lets you lift-and-shift your existing file server to the cloud without changing how your applications access files.
